web_blocks.title: 2.1 Revenue Mix by Product Technology and End-Market

web_blocks.html: Yash Highvoltage is a pure-play maker of condenser-graded transformer bushings [1]. These insulated pathways carry high voltage or current safely through a grounded steel tank wall [1]. Every power transformer needs 5 to 7 bushings, with no technical substitute [1]. In H1 FY27, revenue reached ₹194.5 crore [1]. Resin-Impregnated Paper (RIP) and RIS bushings delivered 86% of product sales, up from 85% in H1 FY26 [1]. Oil-Impregnated Paper (OIP) bushings added 9%, High Current (HC) units added 2%, and specialty products (wall-through, oil-to-oil) added 3% [1].

By channel in H1 FY27, Domestic OEM & Utility sales drove 86% of revenue, down from 91% in H1 FY26 [1]. Exports rose from 5% to 6% [1]. Repair, Retrofit & Testing Services (R&S) doubled its share from 4% to 8% [1]. RIP bushings dominate domestic revenue, but imported core costs have limited RIP exports [1]. Once the Jarod core plant opens in H2 FY27, Yash can export RIP/RIS bushings directly to global markets for the first time [1].

web_blocks.title: 2.2 Concrete End-to-End Real-World Execution Examples by Segment

web_blocks.html: 1. RIP / RIS Condenser Bushings (86% of revenue): Customer & Problem: Central utilities like PGCIL and renewable EPCs build 245 kV substations under strict fire-safety rules. Oil-filled bushings pose explosion risks near expensive power transformers. Engineering & Delivery: Yash builds custom RIP bushings and the 52 kV 6,300 A hybrid STATCOM unit for PGCIL [1]. Workers vacuum-dry crepe paper cores and impregnate them with epoxy resin using Swiss filling machines [1]. Composite silicone sheds house the finished core [1]. Every unit passes 100% partial-discharge (<2 pC) and tan-delta checks in Yash's NABL lab before dispatch [1][2]. This precision supports premium pricing and a 15–18 month order-book cycle [1][2].

2. OIP Condenser Bushings (9% of revenue): Customer & Problem: North American utilities are replacing 40 million aging transformers in earthquake-prone zones [1][3]. They face 2+ year OEM lead times and need IEEE C57.19-compliant 138 kV and 230 kV bushings that will not leak oil [1][3]. Engineering & Delivery: Yash winds craft paper and aluminum foil cores on high-speed machines and cures them in SCADA vacuum autoclaves [1]. Every OIP unit undergoes a 16-hour oil pressure test at 1.8 kg/cm² with tan-delta <0.4% [1]. In H1 FY27, Yash became the first Indian OEM to pass US seismic tests [1]. It now markets IEEE OIP bushings across 27 US states through Yash HV USA Inc. [1][5].

3. High Current (HC) & Wall-Through Bushings (5% combined): Customer & Problem: Large thermal, hydro, and nuclear generator step-up (GSU) transformers carry 4,000 A to 25,000 A at 24–52 kV without overheating [1][3]. GIS-to-transformer halls also need 245 kV wall-through bushings [1][3]. Engineering & Delivery: In 2024, Yash won India's first 25,000 A HC bushing order [1]. In H1 FY27, it tested in-house and shipped its first 245 kV wall-through bushing to a major Indian PSU [1][3]. Few global peers match this custom thermal and cantilever design skill.

4. Repair, Retrofit & Testing Services (8% of revenue): Customer & Problem: State utilities operate 20-to-30-year-old transformers with leaking European OIP bushings whose spares are discontinued [1]. Replacing an entire transformer costs crores and causes months of downtime. Engineering & Delivery: Yash's field team runs on-site Capacitance and Tan-Delta diagnostics and measures flange dimensions [1]. It then supplies a drop-in 145 kV or 245 kV RIP retrofit, with 900+ retrofits completed to date [1]. Utilities upgrade to fire-safe dry RIP bushings in days, giving Yash high-margin recurring revenue.

web_blocks.title: 2.3 Technical Engineering Depth Across Product Lines

web_blocks.html: Yash's engineering moat rests on capacitive-grading precision across all four segments [1]. Workers interleave aluminum foil layers inside paper windings to smooth electric-field stress from the conductor to the flange [1]. In OIP bushings (15–245 kV, up to 3,150 A), Yash guarantees tangent delta below 0.4% at 50/60 Hz [1]. Every unit also passes a 16-hour oil pressure test at 1.8 kg/cm² to confirm zero micro-leaks [1]. Dry-type RIP/RIS bushings (24–245 kV, 400–3,150 A, with 550 kV in development) remove mineral oil completely [1]. This design cuts weight by 30–40%, permits horizontal or vertical mounting, and removes fire risk indoors [1].

Customizability prevents commoditization. Beyond standard catalog ratings, Yash builds custom current ratings above 3,150 A, wall-through bushings (24–245 kV), and HC units up to 25,000 A (24–52 kV) [1]. Every transformer OEM uses slightly different tank turrets, creepage distances, and draw-rod interfaces. Yash turns around custom drawings fast, backed by 130+ years of senior-team engineering experience [1]. That speed locks in repeat orders across more than 1,000 customers [1].

book_paragraphs: If you want to understand why Yash Highvoltage earns 48% gross margins on an industrial electrical component, you have to picture what a condenser bushing actually does. A power transformer sits inside a grounded steel tank filled with insulating oil, yet it must bring 245,000 volts—or 25,000 amperes of current—out of that tank and onto overhead transmission lines without arcing to the steel wall. Every transformer needs five to seven of these bushings, and there is no workaround.

Yash's revenue is concentrated in four distinct product lines, led overwhelmingly by Resin-Impregnated Paper (RIP) and RIS bushings at 86% of H1 FY27 turnover. Why has RIP taken over? Because in a traditional Oil-Impregnated Paper (OIP) bushing, the core is bathed in mineral oil inside a brittle porcelain shell. If a fault occurs, porcelain shatters and oil sprays onto a hot transformer—an instant substation fire. An RIP bushing replaces the oil with solid cured epoxy resin and the porcelain with lightweight silicone-polymer sheds. It is maintenance-free, 30–40% lighter, and fire-retardant.

Yet OIP bushings—9% of revenue—are far from obsolete. In North America, where 40 million transformers are operating past their design life, IEEE-standard OIP bushings remain the workhorse for grid replacement. In H1 FY27, Yash became the first Indian OEM to pass stringent seismic qualification for 138 kV and 230 kV IEEE OIP bushings, giving it an immediate wedge into 27 US states where lead times for domestic American transformers exceed two years.

book_subsections.title: The Hidden Gem: Retrofits, High-Current Customs, and Aftermarket Stickiness
paragraphs: Look closely at the remaining pieces of the pie: High Current bushings (2%), specialized wall-through and oil-to-oil bushings (3%), and Repair, Retrofit & Testing Services, which doubled from 4% to 8% of revenue in H1 FY27. In high-current generator step-up applications—up to 25,000 amperes—Yash is not competing on catalog price; it is solving thermal-dissipation problems for nuclear, hydro, and thermal power stations.

And in retrofits, Yash has built a quiet annuity. When a state utility in Gujarat or West Bengal has a 25-year-old transformer whose original European bushing is weeping oil and spares are no longer manufactured, Yash's engineers measure the existing turret on-site and build a drop-in 145 kV or 245 kV RIP replacement. Over 900 transformers have been retrofitted this way, turning an aging grid into a high-margin service business.

callouts.text: When a service and retrofit division doubles its share of revenue from 4% to 8% during a 95% top-line surge, it tells you that customers are not just buying hardware—they are outsourcing substation reliability to Yash's engineers.

book_subsections.title: Why 5–7 Bushings Per Transformer Creates Asymmetric Stickiness
paragraphs: Let us pause on the unit economics of a power transformer from the customer's perspective. A large 245 kV power transformer is a multi-crore piece of capital equipment, and every single unit requires five to seven bushings—three high-voltage phase bushings, a neutral bushing, and secondary or tertiary bushings. If a single bushing experiences partial discharge or moisture ingress, the resulting arc can destroy the entire transformer and knock out a regional substation.

That is why transformer OEMs do not shop for bushings the way they shop for standard fasteners or mild steel. They want guaranteed tangent delta below 0.4%, partial discharge testing below 2 picocoulombs, and 100% 16-hour pressure testing before a unit ever leaves Vadodara. By offering both IEC and IEEE standards, silicone-polymer and porcelain housings, and custom ratings up to 25,000 amperes, Yash has positioned itself as a single-window technical partner rather than a low-bid vendor.

book_subsections.title: The Strategic Value of the 245 kV Wall-Through and Seismic IEEE Milestones
paragraphs: Two milestones from H1 FY27 illustrate how Yash keeps widening its product moat. First, the company tested in-house and delivered its first 245 kV wall-through transformer bushing to a premier Indian public sector undertaking. Wall-through bushings carry high-voltage conductors directly through substation building walls into gas-insulated switchgear halls—an application with tight mechanical and dielectric tolerances.

Second, Yash became the first Indian OEM to complete stringent seismic qualification testing on IEEE-compliant 138 kV and 230 kV OIP condenser bushings. In seismically active regions of the Western United States and South America, utilities will not even consider a bushing without IEEE seismic certification. Clearing that hurdle turns Yash's 27-state US sales representation network from a brochure exercise into a qualified bidding machine.
